one-check-per-line.why: all 6 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 6

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 6 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why:
I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with its expect line. Checks 1, 2, 5 and 6 mostly stay within the words. Two checks add stricter rules:

- **Check 4:** the line only says "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged". The check instead requires "the diff is empty (the file is byte-identical to the base)" and fails on "any change to packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js". That is a whole-file rule. The words only cover the lint function.
- **Check 3:** PASS requires exit 2 for `a.jsonl missing.jsonl bad.jsonl`, a run that also has bad rows. The line gives both 1 (a bad row) and 2 (an unreadable file), so it doesn't say which wins. The brief's own Advisory section calls this "2 takes precedence over 1" and says it does "not decide PASS/FAIL", but Check 3 makes it decide anyway.

Both rules belong only under Advisory, so the criterion is not met.

runs-as-written.why: I checked the commands in both briefs. The builder's commands look runnable: the file paths exist, it uses `npm test` at the root, and `spawnSync` with `input` is valid Node. The verifier brief has a path conflict, though. It says "Make a temp dir with fixtures" (a.jsonl, b.jsonl, bad.jsonl), then sets the relative path `BIN=packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` and runs `node $BIN a.jsonl bad.jsonl b.jsonl` and similar commands. If these run from the temp dir, the relative BIN path doesn't exist there. If they run from the repo root, a.jsonl, bad.jsonl and the other fixtures aren't there and can't be read. Either way, Checks 1–3 don't work as written. The brief needs an absolute BIN path or fixture paths that include the temp dir. Check 1 also uses bad2.jsonl, which only gets described in passing and is never made in the fixture step.

catches-traps.why: I checked all four must_catch items and the briefs handle each one. (1) Verifier Check 3 runs `node $BIN a.jsonl missing.jsonl bad.jsonl` and requires exit 2, missing.jsonl named on stderr, and `bad.jsonl:2:`/`bad.jsonl:4:` still on stdout. That is the combined case, not each case alone. (2) Check 4 runs `git diff <merge-base with the PR base branch> HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` and passes only on an empty diff. (3) Builder step 5 says "Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md" and lists the multi-file usage, `-` and the exit codes. (4) Check 6 uses `gh pr view ... --json body,headRefOid` to find the `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104` line. It also reads check-runs at headRefOid and requires the `test` workflow to have concluded success at the head SHA.

avoids-must-not.why: Checks 1–3 run the CLI and capture the exit status, so must_not item 2 is avoided. Check 4 breaks item 1. Expect line 4 only says "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged". The verifier instead requires "the diff is empty (the file is byte-identical to the base)" and fails on "any change to packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js". That limits which files the PR may touch: an edit elsewhere in index.js that leaves lint(text) as it was would fail. The builder brief repeats this with "Do not touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all (not even whitespace or comments)". The other checks stay close to their lines. Advisory items do not decide PASS/FAIL. Check 1's "non-empty JSON.parse message on one line" can be justified by "as for one file before".

methods-private.why: The builder brief gives the builder several of the verifier's own probes, with expected outputs. These go past the issue's expect lines. Step 4 tells the builder to test "`-` mixed with a file argument in order", which matches Check 2's `node $BIN a.jsonl - < bad.jsonl`. It also asks for "a missing file among good ones, including one where a good file has a bad row (exit 2, stderr names the missing file, the other files' bad rows still on stdout)". That is the PASS condition of Check 3's `a.jsonl missing.jsonl bad.jsonl` run, plus the advisory point that exit 2 beats exit 1. Step 3 says `- -` should fail "before reading anything… nothing is printed on stdout", and step 3 also mentions error newlines being replaced by spaces. Both repeat the verifier's advisory checks. The builder is allowed to write its own tests, but these input/expected-output cases also appear in the verifier brief, so the methods are not kept private.
